noah: Heads-up — bringing Kitsune-13B (Llama-ish fork with hybrid rotary params) into int4 path. Seeing a reproducible generation regression that looks like a rotary frequency mismatch combined with tokenizer ZWJ/emoji splitting. Repro + tiny logs below. Anyone want to eyeball? :mag:

noah: minimal repro:
```bash
python export.py --model kitsune-13b --format onnx --dtype fp16 --out kitsune_fp16.onnx
python quantize_awq.py --in kitsune_fp16.onnx --out kitsune_int4.onnx --quant-scheme awq --opt axis_swap
python sample.py --model kitsune_int4.onnx --prompt "She said \u200d\u2764\ufe0f loudly" --log-tokens
```

noah: sanitized logs:
```
# fp16 token ids: [3, 44, 23789, 7]
# int4 token ids: [3, 44, 12111, 7]
# first-embed cos_sim: 0.998 -> 0.86
# sample next-token probs changed a lot on the emoji token
```

noah: weird bits: the exporter/quantizer adds an `axis_swap` op to match upstream proj layout. Kitsune uses rotary_freq scale variant (freq_scale != 1.0) and a split-head layout for adapters. If axis_swap assumes uniform head size and implicit freq scaling it can scramble complex-codepoint tokens that live near ZWJ boundaries.

emma: interesting. Does Kitsune use nonstandard rotary base or fractional freq? I recall a fractional freq experiment in that repo. If rotary scaling factor is baked into the projection ordering we could be reinterpreting frequencies when swapping axes.

noah: yes fractional freq = 0.75 in checkpoints (legacy). Also adapter heads are narrower (48) vs main heads (64). axis_swap flattens dims then reshapes assuming 64 heads.

julie: tokenizer side: ZWJ (U+200D) contextualizes emoji joins. If the tokenizer normalization step (NFKC vs NFC) differs between our FP16 stack and quant stack (we run a tokenizer microshim during quant), the multi-codepoint sequence becomes two tokens on int4. The downstream rotary phase alignment then hits a different position and the cos_sim drops.

sam: can you swap quantize flags to skip axis_swap (`--no-axis-swap`) and run token-only diff first? That isolates tokenizer vs weight-ordering.

noah: did that: with `--no-axis-swap` token ids match FP16 for many cases, but logits still drift on composite emoji phrases (RMS next-prob delta ~0.7%). So two effects: (A) axis_swap causes token splitting when combined with the tokenizer microshim, (B) quant rounding + rotary-scale reinterpretation causes small phase drift that amplifies on ZWJ sequences.

emma: plan: 1) add model-registry tag `rotary:fractional` and `heads:hetero` so quant pipeline picks a per-head axis transform rather than global axis_swap; 2) add a tokenizer pre-normalize hook to canonicalize ZWJ-joined emoji to NFC for onboarding runs; 3) add a unit test that runs a short 20-sample emoji bench for any model with fractional rotary or hetero heads.

julie: also double-check the rotary interpolation code path in `rotary_utils.py` during export: when freq_scale != 1.0 we should emit explicit freq constants into the graph (avoid implicit recompute during quant time). If axis transforms reorder those constants you get wrong phases.

sam: good point — emitting explicit freq tensors will make them immune to shallow transposes. I'll prototype emitting `rotary_freq` as a separate initializer and tie it to per-head slices.

ci-bot: [ci] kitsune_int4_onboard_smoke failed  tokenization/regression. https://ci.internal/job/4456

noah: I'll open PR `onboard/kitsune-rotary-compat` with: per-head axis transform in quantizer, explicit rotary_freq initializers in exporter, tokenizer pre-normalize hook, and CI emoji bench. Will attach minimal repro and the CI link.

emma: add a checklist to the PR to run KV-cache smoke tests and a short sampling bench (100 prompts) across FP16/int4 on Hosted and Dedicated. Also include a small script `compare_phases.py` that diffs rotary phase tensors between fp16 and quant outputs.

julie: when you add the tokenizer hook, make it opt-in per-model (onboard-only) so we don't change global behavior without more validation.

noah: ack. early bench (30 prompts) shows: fp16 vs int4 w/ per-head transforms + freq initializers -> BLEU delta 0.4 and token id parity 99.2%. Without those changes BLEU delta 4.2 and parity 85%.

sam: once PR lands we'll run a small canary on Dedicated (10% traffic) and monitor token-level diffs / eval BLEU. I'll coordinate with ops.

ci-bot: created ticket #4820 for kitsune rotary compatibility tests.

noah: summary in PR: root causes = global `axis_swap` + fractional rotary freq baked in + tokenizer microshim normalization; fixes = per-head axis transforms, explicit rotary_freq initializers, opt-in tokenizer NFC pre-normalize, CI emoji bench. Opening PR now. :rocket:
